about: What README.md and the docs/data-sources pages say about each metro area in areas.json (Packages/CatchCore/Sources/TransitCore/Resources). tools/generate_area_docs.py writes them from this file, areas.json, source-list.json and area_counties.bin. Per area: "covers" (what it covers, for its page and the list in docs/data-sources.md; README.md gives only the number of areas), "inText" (how a sentence names it when that isn't "the" and its name, as "Greater Boston"), "label" (where its name is written on the map: [latitude, longitude]; the map picks each area's color itself, from a fixed set that can be told apart with any kind of color vision, so that neighbors differ), "places" (towns labeled on the map: [name, latitude, longitude], or with "left" or "above" to put the name left of or above its dot; the first is larger) and "groups" (its page's operator tables; each row names the areas.json operators it covers in "ops", and every operator of the area must be in one of its rows). "keys": how to get each key or account, on the page of every area with an operator that needs it. "rules": the rules docs/metro-areas.md starts with, which say how every area's counties are chosen; per area, "official" is the US government's metro area it starts from ("name" as a sentence names it, and its "counties"), "added" and "leftOut" the counties put in or left out, each group with the "text" saying which and why (citing the rule), and the check makes sure the official counties, plus those added, minus those left out, are the area's counties in areas.json. "positions": where the positions of each operator's stations without times come from (see the data sources page).

rules.title: Whole counties
rules.text: Each metro area is a list of whole counties. In Connecticut, which replaced its counties with planning regions in 2022, it is a list of planning regions.

rules.title: The government's metro areas first
rules.text: An area starts from the US government's own metro area around its city, as defined by the Office of Management and Budget in OMB Bulletin 23-01: the combined statistical area, which joins neighboring metro areas that many people commute between, or the metropolitan statistical area where there is no combined one.

rules.title: Names from Wikipedia
rules.text: An area is called by the name of its English Wikipedia article, such as Greater Boston or Lehigh Valley, rather than by the government's long list of cities.

rules.title: Islands
rules.text: A county that can only be reached by boat, where the boats leave from a metro area, is part of that area, even where the government leaves it out.

rules.title: Changes
rules.text: Where the government's area doesn't match where people travel, a county can move to the next area, and an area can be split in two or joined with its neighbor. Each area below says what changed and why.

rules.title: Where the app works
rules.text: Only in an area's counties, and there near its trains, buses and ferries: the far parts of large rural counties, at the service area's outer edge, are outside it, and the map in the README shows only the parts inside. A part of an area's counties that lies between two parts of the service area is in too, even with no stop nearby, so the service area has no holes: Salisbury, Connecticut, and Sheffield, Massachusetts, are in for that reason. A pier or a boat on the water, which is in no county, counts in the nearest one. Where you are, or a place you pick, still counts up to 15 km beyond the service area, in the nearest of the areas' counties, so the app doesn't say you are outside just over its edge.

rules.title: Edges
rules.text: Where an area's own buses or trains run into the next county, that county is added to the area, and only the part near their stops is in the service area.

rules.title: One piece
rules.text: Each area is one piece, drawn on the app's map as a single dashed ring. Where an area has islands off its coast, the water between them and the mainland is in the service area too, and over the water the edge runs in straight lines that line up with the edge beside them, with no notches. Only water is added to join the pieces: no county and no stop.

keys.text: **MTA Bus Time key** (MTA bus real-time data): open the [MTA Bus Time sign-up page](https://register.developer.obanyc.com/), enter your name and email, and MTA emails you the key. Paste it in **Settings → Data source → Keys and accounts**. MTA bus times are live only, so without the key no MTA bus times are shown.

**NJ Transit developer account** (NJ Transit rail and bus real-time data): sign up on the [NJ Transit developer site](https://developer.njtransit.com/registration) and select the GTFS-RAIL and GTFS-BUS APIs. NJ Transit reviews each request and emails you when the account is approved. Enter the same username and password in **Settings → Data source → Keys and accounts**, with the username written exactly as the developer site shows it at the top right and the approval email writes it, including capital letters.

**Swiftly key** (Suffolk County Transit real-time data): fill in the [Swiftly request form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScy9Jye91QPSTS3WVEU-13es0A1rT9Ep5JhAmXUZEiop7fmIw/viewform) linked from Suffolk County's website, choosing Suffolk County Transit and GTFS-Realtime Trip Updates. Swiftly reviews each request and emails you the key. Paste it in **Settings → Data source → Keys and accounts**.
